applicant_utility.summary: Up to 76 awards of €8,000 gross a year plus a student-fee waiver for international students admitted to an English-taught Padua degree, paid in two €4,000 instalments, and available across English-taught including single-cycle second-cycle programmes. Because there is no scholarship application, the whole competition is your degree application, so the deadline that matters is the admission deadline of the programme you choose and applying in the first call is a real advantage. You must be ready to accept both offers and to move your residence to Padua with an Italian or SEPA IBAN before any cash reaches you.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Non-Italian, non-Italy-resident applicants with an outstanding academic record applying in the first admission call to an English-taught Padua degree, including single-cycle second-cycle programmes.
application_readiness_checklist: Confirm that your chosen programme is listed as English-taught in the relevant call, including whether it is a single-cycle second-cycle programme
Apply within the first call for admission, because Teaching Committees start from first-call applicants and only use later calls if places remain
Prepare to accept the admission offer and the scholarship offer separately, since declining either loses the award
Plan the transfer of residence to Padua and open an Italian or SEPA bank account, or a prepaid card in your own or joint name
Reserve the regional fee and the revenue stamp for each academic year
common_rejection_risks: Applying only in a later call, which pushes you behind first-call applicants
Holding Italian citizenship, including dual citizenship, or currently residing in Italy
Failing to accept both the admission offer and the scholarship offer
Earning fewer than 20 credits by 30 November of the following academic year, which revokes the scholarship
Transferring to another degree programme or university, or withdrawing from studies, which obliges repayment of the amount received
Being unable to provide an Italian or SEPA IBAN, which blocks disbursement
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: The regional fee and revenue stamp for each academic year, living costs in Padua, and travel from home.
document_audit: No separate scholarship file, essay or reference is required - the degree application is the only file
The non-Italian secondary diploma or non-Italian academic qualification requirement applies at application stage, matching the non-Italian citizenship rule
alerts: The 2027/28 call is expected in November 2026 with a first application window closing on 15 November 2026, which is a narrow turnaround for such a substantial award
Results are published on the University website rather than sent individually
The 20-credit rule is absolute: fewer than 20 CFU by 30 November revokes the award even after the first instalment has been paid
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Apply to the English-taught degree within its admission deadline, check the University's admissions results page for the Teaching Committee ranking, accept both the admission and the scholarship, then transfer residence to Padua and register an IBAN to begin receiving the €4,000 instalments.

official.deadline_note: The Ministry does not publish a closing date on the ITALYOU page. The selection process for scholarship recipients is coordinated by the University for Foreigners of Perugia with the support of its Partner institutions in each target country, and Italian diplomatic missions in those countries play an active role through designated representatives, so the closing date is communicated through those channels. Successful candidates begin on 1 October 2026 for the a.y. 2026-2027 fourth edition.

applicant_utility.summary: A ministry-funded MAECI scholarship of €8,000 for one academic year, paid in 12 monthly instalments, to study the ItAS master's in Italian for Teaching to Foreigners at the University for Foreigners of Perugia. It is a cultural diplomacy instrument of the Mattei Plan for Africa, designed explicitly to produce Italian teachers in the graduates' home countries, so the intended career path of teaching Italian abroad should be visible in your motivation. Selection is run by Perugia with its partner institutions and designated representatives of the Italian diplomatic mission in your country, which means the route to an application is local and personal rather than a portal you can simply download.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Young graduates from Algeria, Cameroon, Egypt, Ethiopia, Libya, Morocco, Senegal, Somalia, South Africa or Tunisia who want to teach Italian and can commit to the ItAS master's in Perugia.
application_readiness_checklist: Contact the University for Foreigners of Perugia directly, since the selection process it coordinates is the only route and it is not a MAECI online portal application

Check with the Italian diplomatic mission or its designated representative in your country whether your country is in the current edition, since the 4th edition lists seven countries while the programme page lists ten
Prepare a motivation that makes explicit your intention to teach Italian in your country of origin, which is the stated purpose of the programme
Confirm you can enrol in the ItAS master's at Perugia, since the scholarship is tied to that specific programme
If you hold a scholarship from the 3rd edition, confirm you have passed exams worth at least 40 CFU to renew for a.y. 2026-2027
common_rejection_risks: Coming from a country not included in the edition in force, since the country list has varied from ten countries to seven
Applying to the Ministry rather than to the university-run selection process, which delays you past the local deadlines
Missing the locally communicated closing date, since the Ministry does not publish one on the ITALYOU page
Failing to secure a place on the ItAS master's, without which the scholarship cannot be used
For 3rd-edition holders, not reaching 40 CFU, which blocks renewal
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: The Ministry page does not state what the €8,000 covers, so tuition, accommodation, flights and living costs should all be budgeted from the €8,000 until the selection process confirms otherwise.
document_audit: The document set is defined by the selection process coordinated by the University for Foreigners of Perugia rather than published on the Ministry page
The programme is run in collaboration with the University for Foreigners of Perugia, so university-level admission documents are part of the file
The renewal rule is a credit threshold of at least 40 CFU, which is unusually explicit for a third-year continuation
alerts: The 4th edition opens with awards starting 1 October 2026, so the local selection must have concluded by late summer
64 students from the 3rd edition renewed for 2026-2027, which shows the scheme is continuing rather than one-off
Because it sits inside the Mattei Plan for Africa, the programme's profile and country coverage may shift between editions, so verify the current list rather than relying on this record alone
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Approach the University for Foreigners of Perugia and its partner institution in your country to learn the local deadline and document set, complete the selection coordinated by Perugia with the Italian diplomatic mission involved, then enrol in the ItAS master's for the 1 October 2026 start.
